modules.name: quic
modules.desc:
Source Code: lib/quic.js

The 'node:quic' module provides an implementation of the QUIC protocol. To access it, start Node.js with the --experimental-quic option and:

import quic from 'node:quic';

const quic = require('node:quic');

The module is only available under the node: scheme.

methods.name: connect
methods.desc:
Initiate a new client-side session.

import { connect } from 'node:quic';
import { Buffer } from 'node:buffer';

const enc = new TextEncoder();
const alpn = 'foo';
const client = await connect('123.123.123.123:8888', { alpn });
await client.createUnidirectionalStream({
  body: enc.encode('hello world'),
});

By default, every call to connect(...) will create a new local QuicEndpoint instance bound to a new random local IP port. To specify the exact local address to use, or to multiplex multiple QUIC sessions over a single local port, pass the endpoint option with either a QuicEndpoint or EndpointOptions as the argument.

import { QuicEndpoint, connect } from 'node:quic';

const endpoint = new QuicEndpoint({
  address: '127.0.0.1:1234',
});

const client = await connect('123.123.123.123:8888', { endpoint });

methods.name: listen
methods.desc:
Configures the endpoint to listen as a server. When a new session is initiated by a remote peer, the given onsession callback will be invoked with the created session.

import { listen } from 'node:quic';

const endpoint = await listen((session) => {
  // ... handle the session
});

// Closing the endpoint allows any sessions open when close is called
// to complete naturally while preventing new sessions from being
// initiated. Once all existing sessions have finished, the endpoint
// will be destroyed. The call returns a promise that is resolved once
// the endpoint is destroyed.
await endpoint.close();

By default, every call to listen(...) will create a new local QuicEndpoint instance bound to a new random local IP port. To specify the exact local address to use, or to multiplex multiple QUIC sessions over a single local port, pass the endpoint option with either a QuicEndpoint or EndpointOptions as the argument.

At most, any single QuicEndpoint can only be configured to listen as a server once.

classes.name: QuicEndpoint
classes.desc: A QuicEndpoint encapsulates the local UDP-port binding for QUIC. It can be used as both a client and a server.

properties.name: address
properties.desc:
The local UDP socket address to which the endpoint is bound, if any.

If the endpoint is not currently bound then the value will be undefined. Read only.

properties.name: busy
properties.desc:
When endpoint.busy is set to true, the endpoint will temporarily reject new sessions from being created. Read/write.

// Mark the endpoint busy. New sessions will be prevented.
endpoint.busy = true;

// Mark the endpoint free. New session will be allowed.
endpoint.busy = false;

The busy property is useful when the endpoint is under heavy load and needs to temporarily reject new sessions while it catches up.

properties.name: closed
properties.desc: A promise that is fulfilled when the endpoint is destroyed. This will be the same promise that is returned by the endpoint.close() function. Read only.

properties.name: closing
properties.desc: True if endpoint.close() has been called and closing the endpoint has not yet completed. Read only.

properties.name: destroyed
properties.desc: True if endpoint.destroy() has been called. Read only.

properties.name: stats
properties.desc: The statistics collected for an active session. Read only.

methods.name: close
methods.desc:
Gracefully close the endpoint. The endpoint will close and destroy itself when all currently open sessions close. Once called, new sessions will be rejected.

Returns a promise that is fulfilled when the endpoint is destroyed.

methods.name: destroy
methods.desc: Forcefully closes the endpoint by forcing all open sessions to be immediately closed.

methods.name: [Symbol.asyncDispose]
methods.desc: Calls endpoint.close() and returns a promise that fulfills when the endpoint has closed.

classes.name: QuicSession
classes.desc: A QuicSession represents the local side of a QUIC connection.

methods.name: close
methods.desc: Initiate a graceful close of the session. Existing streams will be allowed to complete but no new streams will be opened. Once all streams have closed, the session will be destroyed. The returned promise will be fulfilled once the session has been destroyed.

methods.name: destroy
methods.desc: Immediately destroy the session. All streams will be destroys and the session will be closed.

methods.name: createBidirectionalStream
methods.desc: Open a new bidirectional stream. If the body option is not specified, the outgoing stream will be half-closed.

methods.name: createUnidirectionalStream
methods.desc: Open a new unidirectional stream. If the body option is not specified, the outgoing stream will be closed.

methods.name: sendDatagram
methods.desc: Sends an unreliable datagram to the remote peer, returning the datagram ID. If the datagram payload is specified as an ArrayBufferView, then ownership of that view will be transfered to the underlying stream.

methods.name: updateKey
methods.desc: Initiate a key update for the session.

methods.name: [Symbol.asyncDispose]
methods.desc: Calls session.close() and returns a promise that fulfills when the session has closed.

modules.name: type:_`endpointoptions`
modules.desc:
• <Object>

The endpoint configuration options passed when constructing a new QuicEndpoint instance.

properties.textRaw: `address` {net.SocketAddress | string} The local UDP address and port the endpoint should bind to.
properties.name: address
properties.desc: If not specified the endpoint will bind to IPv4 localhost on a random port.
properties.shortDesc: The local UDP address and port the endpoint should bind to.

properties.name: addressLRUSize
properties.desc: The endpoint maintains an internal cache of validated socket addresses as a performance optimization. This option sets the maximum number of addresses that are cache. This is an advanced option that users typically won't have need to specify.

properties.name: ipv6Only
properties.desc: When true, indicates that the endpoint should bind only to IPv6 addresses.

properties.name: maxConnectionsPerHost
properties.desc: Specifies the maximum number of concurrent sessions allowed per remote peer address.

properties.name: maxConnectionsTotal
properties.desc: Specifies the maximum total number of concurrent sessions.

properties.name: maxRetries
properties.desc: Specifies the maximum number of QUIC retry attempts allowed per remote peer address.

properties.name: maxStatelessResetsPerHost
properties.desc: Specifies the maximum number of stateless resets that are allowed per remote peer address.

properties.name: retryTokenExpiration
properties.desc: Specifies the length of time a QUIC retry token is considered valid.

properties.name: resetTokenSecret
properties.desc: Specifies the 16-byte secret used to generate QUIC retry tokens.

properties.name: tokenExpiration
properties.desc: Specifies the length of time a QUIC token is considered valid.

properties.name: tokenSecret
properties.desc: Specifies the 16-byte secret used to generate QUIC tokens.

properties.name: validateAddress
properties.desc: When true, requires that the endpoint validate peer addresses using retry packets while establishing a new connection.

properties.name: alpn
properties.desc: The ALPN protocol identifier.

properties.name: ca
properties.desc: The CA certificates to use for sessions.

properties.name: cc
properties.desc:
Specifies the congestion control algorithm that will be used . Must be set to one of either 'reno', 'cubic', or 'bbr'.

This is an advanced option that users typically won't have need to specify.

properties.name: certs
properties.desc: The TLS certificates to use for sessions.

properties.name: ciphers
properties.desc: The list of supported TLS 1.3 cipher algorithms.

properties.name: crl
properties.desc: The CRL to use for sessions.

properties.name: groups
properties.desc: The list of support TLS 1.3 cipher groups.

properties.name: keylog
properties.desc: True to enable TLS keylogging output.

properties.name: keys
properties.desc: The TLS crypto keys to use for sessions.

properties.name: maxPayloadSize
properties.desc: Specifies the maximum UDP packet payload size.

properties.name: maxStreamWindow
properties.desc: Specifies the maximum stream flow-control window size.

properties.name: maxWindow
properties.desc: Specifies the maxumum session flow-control window size.

properties.name: minVersion
properties.desc: The minimum QUIC version number to allow. This is an advanced option that users typically won't have need to specify.

properties.name: preferredAddressPolicy
properties.desc: When the remote peer advertises a preferred address, this option specifies whether to use it or ignore it.

properties.name: qlog
properties.desc: True if qlog output should be enabled.

properties.textRaw: `sessionTicket` {ArrayBufferView} A session ticket to use for 0RTT session resumption.
properties.name: sessionTicket
properties.desc: A session ticket to use for 0RTT session resumption.

properties.name: handshakeTimeout
properties.desc: Specifies the maximum number of milliseconds a TLS handshake is permitted to take to complete before timing out.

properties.name: sni
properties.desc: The peer server name to target.

properties.name: tlsTrace
properties.desc: True to enable TLS tracing output.

properties.name: transportParams
properties.desc: The QUIC transport parameters to use for the session.

properties.name: unacknowledgedPacketThreshold
properties.desc: Specifies the maximum number of unacknowledged packets a session should allow.

properties.name: verifyClient
properties.desc: True to require verification of TLS client certificate.

properties.name: verifyPrivateKey
properties.desc: True to require private key verification.

properties.name: version
properties.desc: The QUIC version number to use. This is an advanced option that users typically won't have need to specify.

properties.textRaw: `preferredAddressIpv4` {net.SocketAddress} The preferred IPv4 address to advertise.
properties.name: preferredAddressIpv4
properties.desc: The preferred IPv4 address to advertise.

properties.textRaw: `preferredAddressIpv6` {net.SocketAddress} The preferred IPv6 address to advertise.
properties.name: preferredAddressIpv6
properties.desc: The preferred IPv6 address to advertise.
